detail.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61114. Give block verification fresh acceptance and draft random draws when an uncommitted position is revisited in a later round.

## Claims

- Removes the cross-round sampling bias for deterministic and probabilistic drafts in Model Runner V2.
- Keeps standard verification output unchanged and preserves seeded repeat, request-order and batch-splitting behavior in the repaired block path.
- Uses the current round's starting position without adding scheduler state, host synchronization or kernel launches.
- Covers ordinary draft sampling, the shared DFlash2/LiLiCorr candidate walk, DSpark and ordinary watermark fallback.

## Validation

Real V2 generation with one-layer, context-independent Llama target/draft models, TP=1, float32, two speculative tokens and 10,000 requests per configuration:

| Draft | Verification | Expected P(third token = 0) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Deterministic | standard | 0.5000 | 0.5039 | 0.5039 |
| Deterministic | block | 0.5000 | 0.4171 | 0.4954 |
| Probabilistic | standard | 0.3000 | 0.3083 | 0.3083 |
| Probabilistic | block | 0.3000 | 0.3558 | 0.2952 |

All six output marginals pass after the fix; both original block cases fail. Worker types and nonzero acceptance metrics confirm the real V2 draft-model path. Both standard configurations retain identical output hashes before/after. Repaired block runs pass seeded repeat, reordered requests and split batches. The probabilistic block run also passes with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

The new official multi-round regression fails before the fix. Turning off only draft round seeding also fails, showing that acceptance-only repair is insufficient. The mixed watermark test covers the fused ordinary fallback and unchanged raw-logit caching.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_synthetic_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_i64.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_profile.py tests/watermarking --ignore=tests/watermarking/test_engine_compatibility.py --ignore=tests/watermarking/test_watermarking_e2e.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/gumbel.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash2/speculator.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/speculator.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/watermark.py vllm/v1/watermarking/gumbel.py vllm/v1/watermarking/spec_decode.py vllm/v1/watermarking/watermarker.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py tests/watermarking/test_gumbel.py tests/watermarking/test_watermarking.py
git diff --check
```

Results: 355 official tests pass in the CUDA run, with three existing skips; all applicable native hooks pass. Separately, 175 CPU controls pass, with 81 accelerator-dependent skips. The initial nine official watermark model tests also passed. Model tests use Triton attention and a bounded KV cache because this host's driver cannot run the reused CUDA 13 FlashAttention wheel. The candidate-walk tests cover FP32/FP64 round-key parity, conditional proposal-cache contents, padding and CUDA graph replay. DSpark tests fail numerically before flag forwarding is connected; disabling only candidate-walk round seeding also fails numerically. No AMD, full-runner CUDA graph, adaptive-policy model evaluation or throughput claim is made.

## Details

Block verification reads uniforms for draft positions past the finally accepted prefix. Reusing `(request seed, position)` in the next round reuses randomness conditioned on the preceding decision. Probabilistic drafting has the same problem with its position-keyed Gumbel noise.

The existing kernels now mix the round's starting position into the upper 32 bits of the request seed. The rejection kernel reads its first position; the draft kernel subtracts the cached draft step from its source position. The DFlash2/LiLiCorr walk reads the source position before its first candidate, and DSpark forwards the same block-only flag with its existing step column. The position advances after each round, independently of request-slot or batch order. Both ordinary and fused watermark fallback samplers receive that flag; context-keyed watermark draws are unchanged.

Seeded block output intentionally differs from the biased old output, while remaining reproducible in the repaired version. This is distinct from #59355/#60945's residual lookahead bounds and #60652's grammar-invalid drafts, and complements #54282's within-round draft/target stream separation.

Related PR #61153 addresses the same bug. Its implementation passes an explicit round-position tensor and uses a different seed mixer. This implementation derives the key from positions and draft-step metadata already available inside the kernels, avoiding an additional round-position tensor. The same four deterministic/probabilistic, standard/block multi-round distribution cases pass on both implementations, including #61153 at `170dcc217`, using a local argument adapter for its different sampler API. This is an alternative implementation of the same repair, not a claim that #61153 is incorrect.
